details.method: Construct every nested signed test installation from one resolved executable path and use it consistently for argv, broker configuration, and digest. Keep production regular-file and symlink guards intact.
details.when: A deterministic runtime fixture signs an interpreter installation and the host may expose sys.executable through a symbolic link, including normal Python containers.
details.counterexample: Resolving only the outer ordinary-entry interpreter leaves a nested signed-broker argv/config alias invalid. Windows success with a regular executable does not prove the Linux alias case. Production unknown or writable source must not be accepted by relaxing validation.
details.trial_plan: Run the two actual signed and completed-runtime-recovery cases in the normal Linux package from the symlinked interpreter entry; require successful installation, one signed provider-fixture execution and preserved strict installation rejection. Keep old110pass2fail evidence; do not mark this method verified until the exact fixed Linux package passes.
